review: Agree with the writer's reading: the words make अभिलाषु फल-अनुगामी (the wish comes after its fruit, i.e. the fruit is there before the wish); keep the doubt for the owner.
Agree: बिधि as the Creator (विधाता) favourable in every way fits सब बिधि अनुकूल and the context; keep the doubt.
Agree: the subjects are Śrī Rāma and Sītā, whose limbs throb in the previous line, and रामहि बंधु सोच (7.cau4) continues their thought; keep the doubt.

issue: फल अनुगामी ... मन अभिलाषु तुम्हार: does the desire follow the fruit (the fruit comes before the wish) or the fruit follow the desire?
our reading: the desire of your heart follows after its fruit (the words as they stand: अभिलाषु is फल-अनुगामी)
alternatives: the fruit follows your desire, i.e. every wish is at once fulfilled

issue: सब बिधि अनुकूल बिचारि: बिधि as the Creator (fate) or as 'in every way'
our reading: deeming fate (विधाता) favourable in every way
alternatives: considering everything favourable in every respect, with no Creator meant

issue: who are the subjects of परसपर कहहीं: Śrī Rāma and Sītā (from the previous line) or the people
our reading: left as 'they', following the previous line (Śrī Rāma and Sītā)
alternatives: the people of Ayodhyā say this to one another

review: Writer's doubt (whose eyes have their reward): agree; Bharata's eyes (भी) is the plain reading, the alternative is fairly recorded.
Writer's doubt (कुजाती): agree. MW/Apte jāti = birth, caste, and also kind/class; ku-jāti 'of a bad kind' allows the milder 'base-natured'; keep the doubt for the owner.

issue: नयन फलु पावहिं: whose eyes obtain their reward — Bharata's (on seeing the festival) or the citizens' (on seeing Bharata)?
our reading: Bharata comes soon and his eyes too have their reward (seeing the anointing).
alternatives: The people pray that Bharata come soon so that they may have the reward of their eyes in seeing him.

issue: कुजाती: 'of low birth' or 'of base nature'.
our reading: ओछे स्वभाववाली / base-natured (the milder sense the word allows, per style §2).
alternatives: नीच जातिवाली / low-born.

review: Agree: leaving whose heart neutral is right; both readings are possible from the words.
Agree: 'हो चुकी है' covers both readings in Hindi; English 'I have sworn' is the plain reading.

issue: उर पाहन: whose heart is the whetstone, Mantharā's own or Kaikeyī's?
our reading: left as "the stone of her heart" / "हृदयरूपी पत्थर", without naming whose
alternatives: Mantharā's own hard heart (Gita Press Hindi)
Kaikeyī's heart (Gita Press English)

issue: राम सपथ करि आई: did the oath slip out unawares, or was it deliberately sworn?
our reading: the oath has been made (मुझसे शपथ हो गयी / I have sworn)
alternatives: it escaped my lips unintentionally (Gita Press)

issue: भीर: a vocative भीरु (timid one) addressed to Kaikeyī, or भीड़/संकट (in this crisis).
our reading: हे भीरु / Timid one (address).
alternatives: भीर = distress: 'at this hour of distress you cast off trust and love'.

issue: जागति मनहुँ मसानु: 'मसान जगाना' is a cremation-ground rite performed in silence; how far to spell it out.
our reading: as if silently performing the rite of waking the dead (मसान जगाना) in a cremation ground.
alternatives: plainly 'as if awake in a cremation ground' (silent and grim as a burning-ground at night).

review: Agree with the doubt and with the reading बलि = बलिहारी; recorded only so the owner sees the reviewer agrees. The English "Bless you, my son" is a fair rendering of the endearment.
Agree it is a doubt. Our English adds "called the weak" and "grows"; the Hindi is the plain reading. Owner to decide between "a woman once strong" and "a woman, called weak, is strong".

issue: अबला प्रबल: "the weak one (woman) when strong" or "the woman, though called weak, is strong"
our reading: प्रबल हो उठी अबला / a woman, called the weak, once she grows strong
alternatives: अबला कहलानेवाली स्त्री वास्तवमें प्रबल है (a woman, though called weak, is mighty)

issue: बलि: Kaikeyī's endearment (बलिहारी) vs. an oath/adjuration
our reading: मैं तुमपर बलिहारी जाऊँ / Bless you, my son
alternatives: an earnest entreaty: I beg you

review: Agree with the writer's plain reading: line 0 is the lament that line 1 sums up (एहि बिधि बिलपहिं पुर नर नारीं), so leaving the speaker unnamed is right; keep for the owner. No change.

issue: Whose words are line 1: the departing companions' (continuing कहत) or the townspeople's (line 2: एहि बिधि बिलपहिं पुर नर नारीं)?
our reading: Spoken words without naming the speaker; line 2 attributes the lament to the men and women of the city.
alternatives: The companions' parting words, with the townspeople's lament beginning only in line 2.

review: Agree it is a real doubt (सहज सुहृद as a separate person or as qualifying गुर स्वामि); keep the writer's three-person reading for the owner. No change.
Agree: निठुर describes the mother herself (जननी निठुर); keep as a doubt for the owner. No change.

issue: सहज सुहृद: a separate person in the list (a natural well-wisher) or a description of गुर and स्वामि (guru and master who are well-wishers by nature).
our reading: Three persons: a natural well-wisher (friend), a guru and a master.
alternatives: सहज सुहृद qualifies गुर स्वामि: the counsel of a guru and master who wish one well by nature.

issue: जननी निठुर बिसरि जनि जाई: whether निठुर describes the mother (herself) or addresses Rāma.
our reading: Do not forget this hard-hearted mother (Kausalyā calls herself hard-hearted for letting him go).
alternatives: Hard-hearted one (Rāma), do not forget your mother.

review: Agree with the writer's reading (प्रभुहि = Lakṣmaṇa, Tulasīdāsa's Lord); keep as a doubt for the owner. No change.
Agree: keep 'his mother' as the verse says (राम जननि = Kaikeyī); no change to the meaning.

issue: तुलसी प्रभुहि सिख देइ: who is प्रभुहि? Read as Lakṣmaṇa, Tulasīdāsa's Lord, to whom Sumitrā gives the counsel.
our reading: Sumitrā gave this counsel to Lakṣmaṇa, called Tulasīdāsa's Lord (प्रभु लक्ष्मणजीको / his Lord Lakṣmaṇa).
alternatives: प्रभुहि as 'to the Lord' with तुलसी only a signature, i.e. simply 'having counselled the Lord (Lakṣmaṇa)'; same sense, differs only in whether 'Tulasī's' is part of the phrase.

issue: राम जननि: Kaikeyī, Rāma's stepmother, called his mother.
our reading: माताकी सीख / his mother's counsel (Kaikeyī, as the verse says).
alternatives: Could be made explicit as 'his (step)mother Kaikeyī'.

review: A real doubt: MW and Apte give the Aśoka tree as a second sense of शिंशपा and Gita Press reads अशोक; the plain first sense (शीशम) in the meaning is right until the owner decides.

Agree with the writer's reading (the deeds are the bridge): सेतु stands at the end of the clause about चरित, and the line reads most simply so; the other reading (Śrī Rāma himself the bridge) is possible, so the doubt stays for the owner.

issue: तरु सिंसुपा: which tree? Our word meaning and Monier-Williams give शिंशपा as Dalbergia sissoo (शीशम); MW and Apte also give the Aśoka tree as a second sense, and Gita Press reads अशोक.
our reading: शिंशपा (शीशम) का वृक्ष / a śiṃśapā (sissoo) tree
alternatives: अशोकका वृक्ष / an Aśoka tree

issue: संसृति सागर सेतु: is the bridge Śrī Rāma's deeds (चरित) or Śrī Rāma himself?
our reading: The deeds he performs in the manner of men are a bridge across the ocean of worldly existence.
alternatives: Śrī Rāma, himself the bridge across the ocean of worldly existence, performs deeds in the manner of men.

review: Agree with the writer's reading (बाट परना = to be robbed on the road, i.e. lose his livelihood); the doubt can stand for the owner as recorded. No change.

issue: बाट परइ मोरि नाव उड़ाई: बाट परना read as the idiom 'to be robbed on the road' (I would be ruined), with नाव उड़ाई 'my boat would fly away'.
our reading: I would be robbed on the road, and my boat would simply fly away.
alternatives: बाट परइ = 'it would fall in the way (on the road)', i.e. the boat would fly off as it crossed; or 'my livelihood would be stolen'.

review: Agree: 'my own speech' is the plain reading of निज बागीसा in Gaṅgā's mouth; keep the doubt for the owner.
Agree: उतरि is 'having descended' in our word meanings; 'going down to the river' is the plain reading, crossing is the alternative.
Agree: 'whose ways poets cannot know' is the plain reading; the identity question belongs in the doubt only.

issue: सफल होन हित निज बागीसा: बागीसा read as 'my speech' (वाणी) or as Vāgīśa (Brahmā / lord of speech).
our reading: so that my own words (speech) may bear fruit
alternatives: so that my being a goddess of speech may be fruitful; for Brahmā's (Vāgīśa's) word to come true

issue: उतरि: 'having crossed over' the Yamunā, or 'having gone down' into the river.
our reading: going down to the river, they bathed
alternatives: having crossed the Yamunā, they bathed in its water

issue: कबि अलखित गति: whose ways poets cannot know, or that he was a poet (Tulasīdāsa himself, by some) whose identity was hidden.
our reading: poets could not trace his ways
alternatives: he was a poet of unknown identity; his state was unknown to the poet

review: Agree with the writer's reading (Sītā, as mother, knowing him as her child, blessed him); no change.
Agree: बर qualifies बानी (fair speech); 'fully' is not an attested sense of बर. Fix above only rewords the line.
Agree: रूख = tree (the wish-granting tree made a mere tree), the plain reading.

issue: जननि जानि सिसु: who knows whom — the ascetic knowing Sītā as mother, or Sītā knowing him as her child (or both).
our reading: Sītā, as a mother, blessed him knowing him as her child.
alternatives: He placed the dust on his head knowing her as mother, and she blessed him as a child.

issue: बर बानी: whether बर qualifies बानी (excellent speech) or stands apart (बर = fully).
our reading: body, mind and excellent speech grow slack.
alternatives: they become wholly limp in body, mind and speech.

issue: रूख कलपतरु: रूख as 'tree' (made the wish-granting tree a mere tree) or 'dry, harsh'.
our reading: made the wish-granting tree a mere tree.
alternatives: made the wish-granting tree dry/harsh.

review: Agree with leaving it open; our wording ('bound in love') fits both senses of सनेही. No change.
Agree with our reading: सोहीं is 'look', and the distress is already in बिकल; no gloss of grief needed. No change.
Agree: तुम्हहि सहित परिवारा most plainly is the Lord with his household; keep the doubt for the owner. No change.

issue: ए जेहि के सब भाँति सनेही: सनेही can mean 'loving' or 'beloved', so either these princes love that person, or that person loves them.
our reading: Left open: the one to whom these two are bound in love in every way (जिससे इनका सब तरहसे स्नेह है).
alternatives: 'whom these love in every way' (Gita Press: जिसके ये सब प्रकारसे स्नेही हैं); or 'who loves these in every way'.

issue: चकईं साँझ समय जनु सोहीं: the simile is the cakravākī at dusk (about to be parted from her mate); सोहीं literally 'look lovely'.
our reading: They look like female cakravāka birds at dusk (the distress is carried by the first half).
alternatives: Make the grief explicit: as cakravākīs grieve at dusk (Gita Press glosses सोहीं as दुखी हो रही हों).

issue: सहित परिवारा: whose household — the Lord's (his attendants and kin) or the worshipper's.
our reading: worship you together with your household (the Lord's parivāra).
alternatives: they, with their own families, worship you.

review: Agree: speech named at 133.cau2, the bow image in 133.cau1 line 2 as what Lakṣmaṇa saw; cau2 reads on from it naturally.
Agree: मुदित stands next to मुनिबृंदा and qualifies the sages.
Agree with the reading (blessings bear fruit, as Śrī Rāma's success is certain); the alternative is worth the owner's note.

Partly disagree: तोषे is the finite verb and परिपोषे (plural, after बचन) reads most naturally as qualifying the words, 'gentle words nourished with love'; the writer's 'nurtured their love' adds 'their'. Leave for the owner; if the alternative is chosen, Hindi line 1: तब श्रीरामजीने प्रेमसे भरे कोमल वचन कहकर सब वनवासियोंको संतुष्ट किया। / English: Then, speaking gentle words full of love, Śrī Rāma contented all the forest folk.

issue: Where Lakṣmaṇa's words begin: 133.cau3 (अस कहि) shows he spoke the bow image, but the verses name no start; 133.cau1 line 2 could already be his speech.
our reading: 133.cau1 line 2 narration (what Lakṣmaṇa saw); his speech, named, opens at 133.cau2.
alternatives: Speech begins with चहुँ दिसि फिरेउ… in 133.cau1 line 2.

issue: सुफल होन हित आसिष देहीं: whose fruitfulness is meant.
our reading: They bless him so that their blessings may bear fruit.
alternatives: They bless him so that they themselves may be fulfilled (their lives made fruitful).

issue: कहि मृदु बचन प्रेम परिपोषे: whether the words are full of love or the love (of the foresters) is nourished.
our reading: Gentle words that nurtured their love.
alternatives: Gentle words steeped in love (प्रेमसे परिपुष्ट वचन).

issue: मुदित: the sages are glad, or Rāma is glad on seeing them.
our reading: The joyful company of sages.
alternatives: Śrī Rāma, glad to see the sages coming, prostrated.

review: Agree: Lakṣmaṇa serving Sītā and Śrī Rāma is the plain reading (लखनु is the sole subject form); keep the alternative for the owner.
Agree: राउ as the kingship announced gives the joy/sorrow contrast of the next half-line; keep the doubt.
Agree: water alone is the traditional reading (cf. the first night at the Tamasā); keep the doubt.
Agree: तेहि is singular, so 'to him (Sumantra)'; the Hindi उन्हें is honorific and fits.

issue: सेवहिं लखनु सीय रघुबीरहि: who serves whom
our reading: Lakṣmaṇa serves Sītā and Śrī Rāma
alternatives: Lakṣmaṇa and Sītā serve Śrī Rāma (Gita Press gives both)

issue: राउ सुनाइ: राउ as 'kingship' (राज) or 'the king'
our reading: I told him of the kingship (that he would be king) and then gave exile; hence joy/sorrow in the next half
alternatives: राउ = the king (Daśaratha himself) announced the exile

issue: जलपानु करि: water only, or light refreshment
our reading: they stayed on water alone that day
alternatives: they took a light meal (जलपान in the modern sense)

issue: भवनु भयंकरु लाग तेहि: to whom the palace seemed dreadful
our reading: to him (Sumantra)
alternatives: to it / them (the queens' household)

review: Agree with the writer's doubt: the singular बनावा and the narrative favour Śrī Rāma as subject; Gita Press's 'both brothers' (as in Vālmīki) is a fair alternative for the owner.
Agree: तात most naturally stays inside the message to Bharata (the line continues the instructions to him: राखब राऊ); Sumantra as addressee is possible but less likely.
Agree with 'a boat-shaped vessel filled with oil': Vālmīki's tailadroṇī (oil trough) supports it; the plain 'boat' remains the alternative.

issue: जटा मुकुट निज सीस बनावा has a singular verb and names no subject: who made the crown of matted hair, Śrī Rāma alone or Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa both?
our reading: Śrī Rāma (the subject of the verse's narrative, singular verb)
alternatives: Both brothers made crowns of matted hair on their heads (Gita Press)

issue: Whom does तात address in the second half (तात भाँति तेहि राखब राऊ): Bharata, inside Rāma's message, or Sumantra, to whom Rāma is speaking?
our reading: Still Bharata, inside the message (हे तात / Dear one)
alternatives: Sumantra, as Rāma turns back to him

issue: तेल नावँ: an actual boat filled with oil, or a boat-shaped vessel (trough) filled with oil?
our reading: A boat-shaped vessel filled with oil (our word meaning)
alternatives: A boat filled with oil (Gita Press: नावमें तेल भरवाकर)

issue: राम बिरोधी हृदय तें प्रगट कीन्ह बिधि मोहि: either the Creator brought me forth from a heart (Kaikeyī's) hostile to Rāma, or the Creator has shown me to be Rāma's enemy at heart.
our reading: The Creator made me come forth from a heart hostile to Śrī Rāma.
alternatives: The Creator has made me out to be (revealed me as) hostile to Rāma at heart.

issue: रघुबर केतू: केतू may be Ketu the baleful comet/planet, applied to Bharata (I, like Ketu, am the cause), or 'Raghubara, the banner (of the Raghus)'.
our reading: Like the baleful Ketu, I alone am the cause of all these calamities.
alternatives: Śrī Rāma, the banner of the Raghus, is in the forest; I alone am the cause.

issue: राम प्रिय तात तुम्ह: 'Rāma is dear to you' or 'you are dear to Rāma'.
our reading: In word, thought and deed Śrī Rāma has always been dear to you (वचन मन काय describe Bharata's own love).
alternatives: You have always been dear to Śrī Rāma in word, thought and deed (Gita Press Hindi).

issue: जब तैं कुमति कुमत जियँ ठयऊ: कुमति may be an address ('O evil-minded one') or 'with an evil mind'.
our reading: When your evil mind resolved on this evil scheme.
alternatives: O evil-minded woman, when you resolved this evil scheme.

review: Writer's doubt on परम तुम्हार राम कर जानिहि: agree it is worth recording. The plain reading (whoever knows the supreme bond of you and Śrī Rāma; सो = he) fits the correlative सो and is kept; the alternative (Śrī Rāma will know it as your utmost devotion) is a real but less direct reading.

issue: परम तुम्हार राम कर जानिहि: who knows, and what is 'परम'?
our reading: Whoever knows the supreme bond between you and Śrī Rāma will think well of you in every way.
alternatives: Śrī Rāma will know (this) as your utmost (devotion/regard), and he will be pleased with you in every way.

review: Agree with the writer: सहस = स-हास, 'gladly' (MW sahāsa 'accompanied with a laugh'); the doubt can stay for the owner, our reading is right.

issue: करै न सहस सहाइ: is सहस 'gladly' (स-हास) or 'a thousand(fold)' (सहस्र)?
our reading: which does not gladly help one turn towards Śrī Rāma's feet.
alternatives: which does not help a thousandfold / in a thousand ways.

review: Writer's doubt (whose nature shows the love). Agree: our reading (Bharata's natural bearing) is the plain one; the alternative is fair to record.
Writer's doubt (whom the gods praise). Agree: 'him' (उनकी) keeps the verse's तेहि unresolved; record it.

issue: लखब सनेहु सुभायँ सुहाएँ: whose 'nature' — Bharata's bearing, or Guha's own friendly approach?
our reading: His (Bharata's) love will show itself in his natural, gracious bearing.
alternatives: I shall find out his love by approaching him in a natural, pleasing way (Guha's own manner).

issue: सुर सराहि तेहि: whom do the gods praise — Guha, Bharata, or that love?
our reading: Left as 'him' (उनकी), as the verse has it; the next verses praise Guha's fortune in being embraced.
alternatives: Bharata (who embraces him); or the love itself (प्रेम कै रीती).

review: Agree: the plain words leave it open; the meaning rightly does not choose.
Agree with the doubt; the meaning gives the plain words (Tulasīdāsa says … I say it on oath), the reading of the oath is the owner's to settle.
Agree with the reading and the doubt.
Agree: राम सनेहू read as love for Śrī Rāma fits 210.cau1 (राम पेम मृगरूपा); the other reading is fairly recorded.

issue: भइसि प्रान प्रियतम प्रतिकूला: whom did Kaikeyī turn against?
our reading: तू अपने प्राणप्रियतमके ही विरुद्ध हो गयी / You turned against the one dearest to you as life (left open: her husband or Śrī Rāma).
alternatives: Her husband Daśaratha, dearest as life (प्राणप्रियतम पति); or Śrī Rāma, called प्रानपिआरे just before (200.cau1).

issue: तुलसी … कहतु हौं सौंहें किएँ: who takes the oath?
our reading: Tulasī is the poet's signature; the oath (I say it on oath) is Guha's, whose speech goes on.
alternatives: Tulasīdāsa himself vouches on oath that none is as dear to Śrī Rāma as Bharata.

issue: यहउ कहत भल कहिहि न कोऊ: what is 'this'?
our reading: Even saying this (that Kaikeyī is not to blame) no one will call right, since the wise hold by both world and Veda.
alternatives: No one will think well of Kaikeyī even if I say this; or 'this' is the sage's own excusing of her, which world and Veda would not support.

issue: धरें देह जनु राम सनेहू: love for Śrī Rāma, or Śrī Rāma's love?
our reading: You are love for Śrī Rāma embodied (श्रीराम-प्रेम).
alternatives: You are Śrī Rāma's own love for his devotees in bodily form.

review: Agree: बिसमय is विस्मय (MW: wonder, also bewilderment, perplexity); keep 'wonder' in the text and the doubt for the owner.
Agree with the reading (Guha tells it in gentle words) and with recording the doubt.
Agree: बहुरि continues प्रथमहिं of 214.cau4; lodgings to Bharata last by the sage's order.
Agree with the reading and the doubt.

issue: हरष बिसमय बस लोगा: is बिसमय wonder (विस्मय) or dismay (विषाद)?
our reading: joy and wonder (MW/Apte vismaya: wonder, amazement, perplexity).
alternatives: Joy and dismay: joy at the sage's power, dismay that men under vows in Śrī Rāma's absence are offered such pleasures (fits the cakavā image of 215.do).

issue: पूँछत सखहि कहत मृदु बानी: who speaks in gentle words?
our reading: Bharata asks the friend, and Guha tells it in gentle words.
alternatives: Bharata asks the friend, speaking in gentle words himself.

issue: बहुरि सपरिजन भरत कहुँ रिषि अस आयसु दीन्ह: lodgings given to Bharata last, or the sage's instruction to Bharata?
our reading: After everyone else, Bharata and his household were given their lodging, for the sage had so ordered (continuing 214.cau4 प्रथमहिं बास दिए सब केही).
alternatives: Then the sage gave Bharata and his household such instructions (to go and stay).

issue: तेहिं हमार हित कीन्ह बँसूला: what is made the adze?
our reading: The evil counsel made our own good (the coming coronation) into its adze.
alternatives: It made an adze to cut down our good.

review: Agree with the writer's reading: लागी is feminine, and सुभागी at the rhyme describes the woman who speaks. Keep the doubt for the owner.
Agree: नाथ is left unnamed and तन may be Bharata's or the company's; the plain reading (the company, from separation from their lord) is fair. Keep the doubt.

Agree it is a doubt, but the alternative (चित हित थिति: a footing for his mind, हित = for; MW sthiti: standing firm, stability) is the more usual reading and fits cau3's समाधान; the owner should weigh it. The fix above keeps the writer's reading and only drops the added concession.

issue: सील सनेह सुभाय सुभागी: is सुभागी the fortunate woman who speaks (agreeing with the feminine लागी), or Bharata, fortunate in conduct, love and nature?
our reading: Then that fortunate woman began to praise Bharata's goodness, his love and his nature.
alternatives: She began to praise Bharata, blessed in his conduct, his love and his nature.

issue: नाथ बियोग ताप तन ताए: whose lord is नाथ, and whose bodies burn? Sītā's dream may show the company burning from separation from Śrī Rāma, or from their dead lord the king (the dream foretells Daśaratha's death).
our reading: Bharata had come with all his company, their bodies burning in the fire of separation from their lord (left unnamed).
alternatives: Bharata's body alone burns with separation from the Lord (Śrī Rāma); or the separation is from King Daśaratha, who has died.

issue: प्रभु चित हित थिति पावत नाहीं: the sense of हित थिति.
our reading: The Lord's mind could not settle where the right course (हित) lay.
alternatives: The Lord's mind finds no place to rest at all (हित as 'for the sake of': no footing for his mind).

review: Agree with the writer's reading (नहिं गुदरत बनई = cannot pass him over), which fits the 'neither … nor' of मिलि न जाइ; the alternative is worth the owner's note.
Agree: 'mindful of their own nature' is the plain reading; the kinship / pledge readings are glosses of the same phrase.

issue: नहिं गुदरत बनई: गुदरना as 'to leave, pass over (ignore)' or as 'to present, report (to the Lord)'
our reading: he can neither go and meet Bharata nor leave him unheeded (our word meaning: छोड़ते, उपेक्षा करते)
alternatives: nor can he refrain from reporting Bharata's arrival to the Lord (गुदरना = निवेदन करना), which he does in 240.cau4

issue: समुझि आपनी ओर: what 'their own side' means
our reading: mindful of their own nature (looking to their own side), they may forgive and honour him
alternatives: considering that Bharata is their own (their kinship), or their own pledge to protect the refuge-seeker

review: Agree with the writer's doubt and reading (the mothers-in-law, gazing at Sītā, grieve); the verse's तिन्ह fits the agent best.
Agree: 'as if the king had died today' fits the lament for Daśaratha just announced.
Agree that the words alone say 'holy water'; the Payasvinī reading is a fair alternative for the owner.
Agree: the line opens the foresters' plea (it follows कहहिं … मृदु बानी and leads into 'you are men of merit').

issue: तिन्ह सिय निरखि निपट दुखु पावा: who sees whom and grieves.
our reading: तिन्ह as agent: the mothers-in-law, gazing at Sītā, were deeply grieved (after Sītā's own view of them in the first half).
alternatives: Sītā, gazing at them (तिन्ह as object), was deeply grieved; the closing half-line then is Sītā's own thought.

issue: मानहुँ राजु अकाजेउ आजू: राजु as 'the king' or 'the kingdom'.
our reading: as if the king had died only today (the lament is for Daśaratha).
alternatives: as if the kingdom had been ruined today.

issue: पावन पयँ: plain 'holy water' or the river Payasvinī by name.
our reading: holy water (the words alone).
alternatives: in the holy Payasvinī (the river at Citrakūṭa), as many commentators read.

issue: मानत साधु पेम पहिचानी: narration or the start of the foresters' plea.
our reading: the start of their speech: the good know love and honour it (a plea not to refuse their gifts).
alternatives: narration: the good citizens, recognising their love, respect them.

review: agree: the grammar (लोह लै = having taken the iron, लौका the subject) gives the writer's reading; Gita Press's 'iron floated carrying the boat' is fairly recorded as the alternative

issue: लोह लै लौका तिरा: which floats, and what is लौका?
our reading: The gourd (लौका) floated carrying iron: लोह लै = having taken iron, लौका the subject of तिरा.
alternatives: Iron floated carrying a boat (लौका = नौका), the iron standing for the lowly forest folk.

review: Writer's doubt (whom नीच describes). Keep it for the owner, but I lean to the alternative: यहउ कहत मोहि आजु न सोभा and cau2 (मातु मंदि मैं साधु … कोटि कुचाली) read as Bharata taking back a word he has just said against his mother, which fits नीच … जननी better. Our reading is allowed by the words.
Writer's doubt (सहाई). Agree with our reading: causative future, matching सहावइ in do262; the alternative is fair to record.

issue: नीच बीचु जननी मिस पारा: whom नीच describes.
our reading: नीच refers to the subject carried from the first half, विधि: the base one (Fate) used the mother as a pretext and made a rift; Bharata goes on (cau2) to call it a crime to think his mother wicked.
alternatives: नीच qualifies जननी: Fate made a rift on the pretext of my vile mother.

issue: जिअत जीव जड़ सबइ सहाई: tense and sense of सहाई.
our reading: Causative future (सहाना): while it lives, this dull soul will make me bear everything (as सहावइ in do262).
alternatives: Present, intransitive: this dull soul, still living, endures it all.

review: Agree: ऐक as अटकल (a gauge, an estimate) fits the boatmen who cannot row it; keep the doubt for the owner.

Disagree with the writer's reading: देखि is an absolutive, so line 3 has no finite verb and its gods, siddhas, ascetics, yogis and sages are the subject of न समरथु कोउ in line 4 (fixes given). Keep the doubt for the owner with the readings swapped.

Disagree: the plain reading is राम गिरि = Śrī Rāma's mountain (Rāmagiri, Citrakūṭa), a list with बन and तापस थल; 'with Śrī Rāma' needs a संग the verse lacks (fixes given). Keep the doubt for the owner with our reading changed to this.

issue: ऐक नहिं आवा: ऐक as अटकल (estimate, gauge) or as एक (not one of them comes forward).
our reading: they cannot even take its measure (no estimate of it comes to them)
alternatives: not a single one (of the boatmen) comes forward / succeeds

issue: Lines 3-4: whether the gods, siddhas etc. are those who could not cross the river of love on seeing Videha's state, or the onlookers of his state while line 4 is Tulasīdāsa's general remark.
our reading: They all saw Videha's state; Tulasīdāsa says no one is able to cross the river of love.
alternatives: Of the gods, siddhas, ascetics, yogis and sages who saw Videha's state, none was able to cross the river of love (Gita Press).

issue: अटनु राम गिरि बन: roaming with Rāma, or roaming on Rāma's mountain (Kāmadanātha) and forests.
our reading: roaming the hills and woods and the haunts of ascetics with Śrī Rāma
alternatives: roaming Śrī Rāma's mountain (Kāmadanātha), its forests and the ascetics' places (Gita Press)

review: Agree it is a doubt, but the meaning should carry one plain reading. MW/Apte sakṛt: 'once, at once, once for all'; no 'seldom'. Our reading: swans in the one Mānasa lake only (the writer's alternative). The 'seldom' reading should be listed as the alternative instead.
reviewer_fix: {"id": "ayodhya.281.do281", "issue": "मानस सकृत मराल: sense of सकृत.", "our reading": "सकृत 'once, only': swans are in the one Mānasa lake only.", "alternatives": "सकृत as 'once in a while': swans are met with only seldom, in the Mānasa lake."}

issue: मानस सकृत मराल: sense of सकृत.
our reading: सकृत "once, seldom": swans are met with only seldom, in the Mānasa lake alone.
alternatives: सकृत as "only one (place)": swans are in the one Mānasa lake only.

review: Agree with the writer's doubt and reading (कहिअ as a polite imperative); the passive reading is a fair alternative for the owner.
Agree: the verse does not say whose love; leaving it as 'the love' is right.
Agree: the impersonal 'shall be taken upon the head' keeps the verse's ambiguity.
Agree: the verse does not name whose mind; Gita Press supplies 'the assembly's'. Leaving it unstated is right.

issue: कहिअ जो आयसु देहु: is कहिअ a request to Bharata or a passive?
our reading: Polite imperative: tell (us) what command you give.
alternatives: Passive: whatever command you give, let it be told (to Śrī Rāma).

issue: करिअ पेमु पहिचानि: whose love is to be recognised?
our reading: Left as the verse has it: recognising the love (Bharata's, in context of his plea).
alternatives: Everyone's love (for Śrī Rāma); or Bharata's own love only.

issue: राउरि सपथ सही सिर सोई: who takes the command upon the head?
our reading: Impersonal, as the verse: it shall truly be taken upon the head.
alternatives: Śrī Rāma himself accepts it; or everyone will bow to it.

issue: सोक कनकलोचन मति छोनी: whose mind did grief carry off?
our reading: Left unstated: the earth of understanding, which Bharata's discernment rescues.
alternatives: The whole assembly's mind; or Bharata's own mind.

review: Agree with the writer's doubt and reading (अतिसय with बिछोहे: 'not wholly cut off'); it is the plain reading of the word order.
Agree: देनी is feminine with बेनी, so साधक is best taken as 'for the one who strives'; the MW adjective sense stays an alternative for the owner.
Agree it is a real doubt: सुभायँ is instrumental of सुभाउ; 'naturally / by the nature of devotion' (ours) and 'by (Bharata's) devotion and good disposition' both fit the grammar.

issue: राम प्रेम अतिसय न बिछोहे: does अतिसय qualify बिछोहे (they were not wholly parted from their love for Rāma) or प्रेम (because of their intense love for Rāma they were not parted from him)?
our reading: अतिसय with बिछोहे: deluded by the gods' māyā, they were still not wholly cut off from their love for Śrī Rāma.
alternatives: Their exceeding love for Śrī Rāma kept them from being separated from him (अतिसय with प्रेम).

issue: साधक एक सकल सिधि देनी: साधक as 'for the one who strives' (देनी is feminine, agreeing with बेनी, so साधक cannot be its adjective) or as the adjective 'accomplishing' (MW sādhaka).
our reading: To one who strives, this alone (obedience) grants every success.
alternatives: This alone accomplishes everything and grants every success (साधक = effective, accomplishing, MW).

issue: भगति सुभायँ सुमति हियँ हुलसी: सुभायँ as 'by the nature of (Bharata's) devotion / naturally', or भगति and सुभाउ as two things (Bharata's devotion and good disposition).
our reading: By the nature of devotion, a good understanding has welled up in the poet's heart.
alternatives: Through Bharata's devotion and good disposition, good understanding swells in the poet's heart.

review: agree with the writer's reading (Sītā, holy in her love for her lord dear as life); the alternative is fairly recorded
agree: धारिअ is the polite request, and देइ असीसा goes most naturally with it (Rāma asks Janaka to bless them and go); the alternative is fairly recorded
agree with leaving the sage unnamed; note for the owner that कौसिक (Viśvāmitra) is named among those present at 319.cau3, which supports मुनि = Viśvāmitra

issue: फिरी प्रानप्रिय प्रेम पुनीता: whose is प्रानप्रिय?
our reading: Sītā returned, pure in her love for her lord (Śrī Rāma), dear to her as life.
alternatives: प्रानप्रिय describes Sītā herself (dear as life to her parents and kin), and प्रेम पुनीता her holy love for them.

issue: पुर पगु धारिअ देइ असीसा: who gives the blessing?
our reading: Part of Śrī Rāma's request: give us your blessing and return to the city.
alternatives: Janaka gives the blessing (देइ असीसा with कीन्ह … गवनु महीसा): giving his blessing, the king steadied himself and departed.

issue: गुर मुनि मिथिलेसू: is मुनि a second person (Viśvāmitra) or the guru himself?
our reading: Three: the guru, the sage and the lord of Mithilā (the sage left unnamed).
alternatives: गुर मुनि = the guru-sage Vasiṣṭha; or मुनि = the sages in general.

review: Agree with the writer's reading (the Lord bowed to the gods and reassured them): प्रभु is the subject of both करि and दीन्ह, and Gita Press reads it so. Keep as recorded.
Agree: निरुपाधि here is 'without hindrance' (Hindi उपाधि 'trouble'); MW's 'without attributes' does not fit an enthronement. Keep as recorded.

Agree: बलु goes with सोई (strength and the beauty of the face stay the same), which fits the autumn simile of 325.cau2. Note for the owner: तेजु here may be the bodily vigour/fat that fasting wears down (MW tejas 'the heating and strengthening faculty of the human frame'); 'lustre' beside an unchanged 'beauty of his face' reads slightly against itself.
Agree: गिरा as Sarasvatī beside Śeṣa and Gaṇeśa, the usual triad of speakers; keep the alternative recorded.

issue: प्रभु प्रनामु करि दीन्ह भरोसो: who bows to whom.
our reading: The Lord bowed to the gods and gave them assurance.
alternatives: The gods bowed to the Lord (प्रभु as object of प्रनामु करि), and he gave them assurance.

issue: निरुपाधि: sense here. MW nir-upādhi "without attributes, absolute"; upādhi "limitation, disguise"; in Hindi उपाधि also "trouble, disturbance".
our reading: Without any hindrance (बिना किसी बाधाके): the sandals were enthroned smoothly.
alternatives: Without reservation or pretence, wholeheartedly; or without any condition or limitation.

issue: घटइ तेजु बलु मुखछबि सोई: whether बलु goes with घटइ or with सोई.
our reading: Lustre wanes, but strength and the beauty of the face stay the same (fits the autumn simile of 325.cau2: water sinks, canes and lotuses thrive).
alternatives: Lustre and strength wane, but the beauty of the face stays the same.

issue: सेस गनेस गिरा गमु नाहीं: गिरा as Sarasvatī or as "speech".
our reading: Śeṣa, Gaṇeśa and Sarasvatī cannot reach there.
alternatives: The speech of Śeṣa and Gaṇeśa cannot reach there.

issue: असमंजस: Sanskrit असमञ्जस (MW, Apte) is 'unbecoming, improper'; Hindi usage is 'dilemma, awkward fix'.
our reading: a boon that leaves me in a quandary (उलझनमें डालता है).
alternatives: an improper, unfitting second boon (the Sanskrit sense).

issue: भामिनी in समुझि धौं जियँ भामिनी
our reading: lady (address to Kaikeyī), MW bhāminī 1: a beautiful woman
alternatives: MW bhāminī 2: an angry or passionate woman (often an endearment and not always separable from sense 1); addressed to Kaikeyī in her sulking-chamber the sense 'angry lady' fits well. Owner to choose between 'lady' and 'angry lady'

issue: पितु बनदेव मातु बनदेवी: बनदेव and बनदेवी carry no number mark; our Hindi and English take them as plural (the gods and goddesses of the forest).
our reading: Plural: the forest gods will be your father and the forest goddesses your mother.
alternatives: Singular: the god of the forest will be your father and the goddess of the forest your mother (वनदेवता पिता, वनदेवी माता).

issue: मिटे दोष दुख दारिद दावा: दावा (Skt दाव: forest fire, heat, distress) as the fire of poverty only, as a fire of all three, or as a fourth item (burning distress).
our reading: my faults and sorrows are gone, and the burning of poverty too
alternatives: the fire of my faults, sorrows and poverty is quenched; faults, sorrow, poverty and burning distress are all erased

issue: अबिगत: Apte gives a-vigata only as 'not gone off, retained, present' (MW vigata 'gone away, disappeared'); neither gives 'unknown'.
our reading: अविज्ञेय | unknowable (the Hindi bhakti sense of अविगत).
alternatives: 'never departing, ever present, imperishable' (the Sanskrit sense: अ-विगत).

issue: सनेही: MW and Apte give snehin only as 'affectionate, attached to, fond of; a friend' (the one who loves), not 'beloved'; this favours 'these two love that one'.
our reading: to whom these two are bound in love in every way; fits the dictionary sense, no change.
alternatives: 'who loves these in every way' is less supported by the dictionaries.

issue: नीलकंठ among the birds: Monier-Williams and Apte give for nīlakaṇṭha the bird senses peacock (first), gallinule, wagtail, sparrow, not the Indian roller; Hindi usage and the commentaries take नीलकंठ पक्षी as the Indian roller (blue jay).
our reading: Blue jays (Indian roller), as in the word suggestion of batch-14.words.jsonl.
alternatives: Peacocks (MW's first bird sense; मोर is not otherwise named in the list).

issue: पितु सुरपुर बन रघुबर केतू: केतू may go with मैं (I, like Ketu the baleful planet, am the cause) or with रघुबर (Rāma, the banner / chief of the Raghus, is in the forest); MW gives केतु 'flag, banner' and 'chief, leader, eminent person', so the second reading is fully supported by the dictionaries.
our reading: Like the baleful Ketu, I alone am the cause of all these calamities.
alternatives: My father is in heaven, Śrī Rāma, banner (crown) of the Raghus, is in the forest; I alone am the cause of every calamity.

issue: जब तैं कुमति कुमत जियँ ठयऊ: तैं is 'you' (as in 161.cau4 पेड़ काटि तैं), the subject of ठयऊ; MW gives कुमति both f. 'vile sentiment, folly' and mfn. 'foolish', so कुमति may be an adjective or address to तैं ('you, evil-minded one') rather than 'with an evil mind'. The English 'your evil mind resolved' makes the mind the subject.
our reading: Hindi: when you, with an evil mind, resolved on this evil scheme; English: when your evil mind resolved on this evil scheme.
alternatives: When you, evil-minded woman, resolved this evil scheme in your heart (English could read: When you, evil-minded one, resolved on this evil scheme, ...).

issue: अँथयउ is a completed past ("has set"); the king dies only in 155, and Gita Press reads "about to set".
our reading: Kausalyā knew in her heart that the sun of the solar line had set (the verb's tense).
alternatives: she knew it was about to set (sense from the context)
